missing_requirements.title: Account Balance Floor Enforcement and Overdraft Prevention
missing_requirements.description: The system must validate that source accounts do not violate minimum balance or overdraft limits prior to committing a debit entry, unless an explicit credit line or overdraft facility is authorized.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: The prompt mandates an atomic financial ledger transaction with debit/credit balance invariance. Step 2: In double-entry bookkeeping, balancing journal entries alone does not prevent individual accounts from dropping below legally or operationally mandated minimums (e.g., negative balances without credit facilities). Step 3: Therefore, a balance floor check must be integrated into the atomic transaction validation phase to maintain account solvency and domain invariants.

missing_requirements.title: Deadlock Prevention and Timeout Guard for Concurrent Ledger Locking
missing_requirements.description: The system must acquire account locks in a deterministic, globally sorted order (e.g., sorting account IDs lexicographically) and enforce strict statement timeouts to prevent circular wait deadlocks during concurrent multi-account transfers.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Concurrent transactions modifying overlapping sets of source and destination accounts under high isolation levels are prone to deadlocks. Step 2: Unmanaged deadlocks lead to transaction aborts, resource exhaustion, and degraded availability. Step 3: Therefore, deterministic lock ordering and timeout guards must be implemented to ensure safe and predictable concurrent execution.

missing_requirements.title: Immutable Ledger Audit Trail and Append-Only Enforcement
missing_requirements.description: The system must prohibit UPDATE and DELETE operations on committed ledger transaction rows, ensuring that any corrections or reversals are executed strictly via compensating entries.
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Financial ledgers require strict regulatory compliance and tamper-evident audit trails. Step 2: Allowing direct modifications or deletions of committed ledger entries destroys historical provenance and breaks double-entry auditability. Step 3: Therefore, the database schema and application logic must enforce append-only immutability for all historical ledger records.
